report.tagline: The video meeting app that became a verb during COVID, now selling phone, chat, contact centre and AI tools to businesses.
report.simpleSummary: Zoom lets you join a video call by clicking a link, with no account needed for guests. During the pandemic, schools, offices and families all used it. Meetings are free for up to 40 minutes, and people or companies pay a monthly fee for longer meetings and extra tools. Now Zoom also sells business phone lines, customer support software and an AI assistant that takes meeting notes.

overview.whatItDoes: Zoom runs video meetings and webinars, and sells a set of work tools called Zoom Workplace: meetings, team chat, phone, whiteboards, docs and scheduling. It also sells Zoom Contact Center for customer support teams. AI Companion, included in paid plans, writes meeting summaries and answers questions.
howItWorks: A host sends a link; guests click and join in the browser or app, often without signing in.
Free users get meetings up to 40 minutes with up to 100 people.
Paid users get longer meetings, cloud recording and AI Companion summaries.
Businesses buy Zoom Phone to replace desk phones, and Zoom Rooms for meeting rooms.
Contact Center and Virtual Agent let companies handle customer calls and chats with AI.
Zoom sells online to small users and through sales teams to large companies.
overview.valueProposition: Video calls that just work: one click to join, good quality on weak internet, and now one vendor for meetings, phone and support.

businessModel.summary: Zoom makes money from subscriptions: individuals and small teams pay monthly online, and companies sign yearly contracts. About 60% now comes from enterprise customers. Growth depends on selling more products, like Phone and Contact Center, to existing customers.

revenueStreams.detail: Pro and Business plans bought by card, by individuals and small teams.
Large companies buying Zoom Workplace, about $741 million a quarter.
Per-agent and usage-based pricing for support teams.
Add-ons for large events and meeting rooms.

businessModel.pricing: Basic: free, 40-minute meetings. Pro: about $13.33 per user per month billed yearly. Business: about $18.33 per user per month billed yearly. Enterprise and Contact Center: custom pricing.
costDrivers: Data centre and cloud costs for video
Sales and marketing, especially for enterprise
AI model costs for AI Companion
Research and development for new products
businessModel.unitEconomics: A Pro user pays about $160 a year. Running their video costs Zoom maybe $20 to $30, so gross margin is high, near 75% to 80% across Zoom. The problem is churn: at about 3% a month, roughly a third of online customers leave each year, so Zoom keeps spending to replace them. An enterprise customer paying $100,000 a year is much stickier, and adding Phone or Contact Center can double that. Rough estimates.

howTheyGetUsers: Every meeting link sent by a host shows Zoom to guests
Free plan with a 40-minute limit that pushes upgrades
Cross-selling Phone and Contact Center to existing customers

growth.moat: Zoom's moat in meetings is thin, because Teams and Google Meet come free with office bundles. Its stronger moat is in the products that are hard to switch, like company phone systems and contact centres, and its brand for reliable calls.

pmLessons: Simplicity can win a market fast: Zoom beat older tools because joining took one click.
A great single feature is easy for big companies to copy and bundle, so you need a second act.
Growth after a boom is hard. Track churn and retention, not just sign-ups from a spike.
Selling more products to existing customers is often cheaper than finding new ones.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you reduce Zoom's online churn?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment who leaves (seasonal tutors, small teams), find why, test pause, annual discounts and value features. Track monthly churn.

interviewQuestions.question: Why did Zoom win in 2020, and why is growth slow now?
interviewQuestions.hint: Simplicity and guest access, then bundles from Microsoft and Google, fewer remote meetings, and churn.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Zoom remove the 40-minute limit?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh more users and goodwill against fewer upgrades. Suggest tests in certain markets.

interviewQuestions.question: How should Zoom compete with Teams?
interviewQuestions.hint: Don't fight on chat. Win on guests, quality, phone and contact centre, and cross-app AI.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a metric for AI Companion's success.
interviewQuestions.hint: Usage share, summaries opened, actions taken, link to renewal and churn.
